content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The specification is drafted and passes all quality checks. **This is the first gate** — per our spec-driven workflow, nothing gets planned or built until you've reviewed and approved this. Please read it as the source of truth for what we're building.

## 📋 Spec ready for review

- **Feature directory**: `specs/001-bookmark-manager/`
- **Spec file**: `specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md`
- **Quality checklist**: all items pass ✅ (no open clarifications)

### What the spec proposes, in plain terms

**Three prioritized user journeys** (each independently shippable):
1. **P1 — Save a bookmark**: paste a web address, it's stored and confirmed. This alone is a usable MVP.
2. **P2 — Browse & find**: search across title/address/notes/tags, and filter by a tag.
3. **P3 — Organize & edit**: edit titles/notes/tags, delete with confirmation.

**Key decisions I made for you** (documented as Assumptions — please confirm or push back):
- **Single user, one device, stored locally** — no accounts, no login, no cloud sync in v1.
- **Manual capture** — you add bookmarks by entering an address in the app; no browser extension or bulk import from browsers yet.
- **Flat tags, not nested folders**, for organization.
- **Best-effort title fetch** — the app tries to grab the page's title, but saving always works even if it can't.

**Success targets**: save a bookmark in <20s; find one among 500 in <5s; nothing lost between sessions.

### Your options at this gate

- ✅ **Approve** → I'll proceed to `speckit-plan` (the implementation plan) for your review.
- ✏️ **Change something** — e.g. "I actually want cloud sync" or "use folders instead of tags" — and I'll revise the spec before we plan.
- ❓ **Clarify** — if any part is ambiguous, I can run a structured clarification pass.

A few things worth your explicit call, since they shape scope the most:
1. Is **local, single-device, no-login** right — or do you need it accessible across devices/browsers?
2. **Tags vs. folders** for organizing?
3. Is **manual entry** fine for v1, or is one-click saving from the browser essential?

How would you like to proceed?

Thanks — this is a good start and mostly matches how I picture it. Let me answer your three questions first, then flag a few things, because I don't think I'm ready to approve just yet.

**Your three questions:**
1. Yes — just me, on my own device, no login. That's right for now.
2. Tags, definitely. Please don't do folders.
3. Manual entry is fine to start. I don't need the browser button yet.

Now the things that gave me pause reading it through:

**Saving:**
- On the duplicate thing — I don't just want a *warning* that it's already saved. When I save a link I already have, I'd expect it to just bring up the existing one so I can tweak it. I don't want two copies, but I also don't want to be stopped with a dead end.
- Grabbing only the title feels thin. When I save something, I'd expect it to pull a bit more on its own — a short description of the page, the little site icon, and a preview picture if it can. Otherwise my list is just a wall of plain text. And I'd want to be able to fix that description myself if it grabs something odd.

**Finding things:**
- I didn't see this spelled out anywhere: when I click a saved bookmark, it should actually open the page. That's really the whole point of keeping them.
- Plain-word search is good, but with a few hundred saved I'd want a little more — searching an exact phrase when I wrap it in quotes, and combining things, like "show me stuff tagged both *recipes* and *dinner*," or one tag but not another. And capitalization shouldn't matter.
- When I'm typing a tag, it'd really help if it suggested tags I've already used, so I don't end up with both "recipe" and "recipes."

**Organizing:**
- Newest-first as the default is fine, but I'd like to sort by title or oldest now and then.
- I'd love to flag some as "read later" and see just those on their own — a lot of what I save is stuff I mean to get back to.
- If I mistype or a link moves, I'd want to fix the address itself too, not only the title and notes.
- And for tidying up — sometimes I don't want to delete something for good, just get it out of my way but keep it around in case. Some way to tuck things aside that's separate from deleting permanently.

Can you fold these in and show me the revised version before we move on to planning?

## 📋 Revised spec ready for review — `specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md`

Here's where your feedback landed:

**Saving**
- **FR-019** — saving an address you already have **opens the existing bookmark for editing**. No duplicate, no dead end. (Also covers editing one bookmark's address into another's.)
- **FR-005 / FR-006** — on save, the app gathers a **description, site icon, and preview image** (best-effort, never blocks the save), and you can **edit the description** if it grabs something odd. Cards show these (FR-007).

**Finding**
- **FR-008** — **clicking a bookmark opens the page**. (This was genuinely missing — good catch.)
- **FR-009/010/011** — search is **case-insensitive**, supports **exact phrases in quotes**, and lets you **combine tags ("all of") and exclude a tag ("not")** — e.g. *recipes* AND *dinner*, or *recipes* NOT *dessert*.
- **FR-012** — **tag suggestions** from tags you've used, so "recipe" and "recipes" don't both spawn.

**Organizing**
- **FR-014** — sort by **newest (default), oldest, or title**.
- **FR-015 / Story 4** — **"read later" flag** with its own dedicated view.
- **FR-013** — you can now **edit the address itself**, alongside title/notes/description/tags.
- **FR-016** — **archive** to tuck items aside (recoverable), kept separate from permanent **delete** (FR-017, still confirmed before removal).

**Also added:** two new success criteria — **SC-006** (≥90% of saves auto-show description + icon for pages that publish preview info) and **SC-007** (zero duplicates, 100% of the time).

The **three answers** you gave are now locked into Assumptions (marked *Confirmed by client*).

A couple of small decisions I made so we're not left guessing at plan time — flag if either is wrong:
- **"Duplicate" means the same address** once normalized (so `example.com` and `https://example.com/` count as the same).
- **Archived items stay out of the main list and default search** — they only show in the archived view.

### Your options
- ✅ **Approve** → I move to `speckit-plan`.
- ✏️ **More changes** → I revise again; we stay at this gate.

Anything else you'd fold in, or shall I proceed to planning?

This is looking really close to what I had in mind — you caught everything I raised, thank you. And your two small calls are both right: yes, treat `example.com` and `https://example.com/` as the same thing, and yes, archived items should stay out of the main list and search unless I go to the archived view.

Just a few more things while I'm looking closely, then I think we're there:

- On search — you gave me "both of these tags" and "this tag but not that one," which is great. But I also sometimes want *either*: show me everything tagged **recipes** *or* **dinner**, even if an item only has one of them. Can I mix those — like "recipes or dinner, but not dessert"?

- When I'm tidying up, doing things one at a time would get tedious. I'd like to pick several bookmarks at once and act on the whole lot together — tag them, archive them, or delete them in one go. Ideally I could even sweep everything currently showing after a search or tag filter.

- Two smaller wishes: if I've built up a search-and-tag combination I use a lot, it'd be nice to save it so I can jump back to it without rebuilding it each time. And when I write notes on a bookmark, I'd like a bit of formatting to show through — headings, bullets, links — rather than one flat block of text.

Fold those in and I think you'll have my approval on the next pass.

Clean — FR-001 through FR-025, no gaps or duplicates. All folded in.

## 📋 Revised spec (pass 2) — `specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md`

Both your confirmations are now baked into Assumptions (normalized-address duplicates; archived items out of main list/search). The four new items:

**Search — "either" is now supported and mixable (FR-011, Story 2)**
- Three tag modes that combine freely: **any of** (`recipes` OR `dinner`), **all of** (both), and **excluding** (NOT `dessert`). Your exact example — *"recipes or dinner, but not dessert"* — is an acceptance scenario.

**Batch actions (FR-019/FR-020, Story 3)**
- Select several bookmarks and **tag / archive / delete the whole batch** in one action (one confirmation for a batch delete).
- **"Select all showing"** sweeps exactly what the current search/filter surfaces — and deliberately *won't* reach hidden or archived items, so a bulk delete can't misfire.

**Saved searches (FR-021, Story 5, new "Saved Search" entity)**
- Name a search+tag combination and jump back to it in one step. It stores the *filter*, not a frozen result list, so it **re-runs live** — newly matching bookmarks show up when you reapply it.

**Rich-text notes (FR-003/FR-018)**
- Notes render **headings, bullet lists, and links** rather than one flat block; unsupported markup degrades to plain text instead of breaking the layout.

Requirements were renumbered cleanly to **FR-001…FR-025**, and the quality checklist still passes with no open clarifications.

### This is the gate
You said this pass would earn your approval. To be explicit before I move on:

- ✅ **Approve** → I proceed to `speckit-plan` and bring the implementation plan back for your review (the next gate).
- ✏️ **More changes** → I revise; we stay here.

Shall I start planning?

This is exactly right — you've captured all of it. The "either/or/not" mix reads just how I'd use it, and I especially like that "select all showing" only touches what's on screen and never reaches into archived stuff, and that a saved search re-runs live rather than freezing an old list. Those were the details I'd have worried about, and they're handled.

✅ **Approved.** Go ahead to planning. I'll see you at the next gate for the implementation plan.

## 🧭 Plan ready for review — the second gate

**Branch**: `001-bookmark-manager` · **Plan**: `specs/001-bookmark-manager/plan.md`
Design artifacts: `research.md`, `data-model.md`, `contracts/rest-api.md`, `contracts/filter-model.md`, `quickstart.md`

Here's the plan in plain terms — the main thing for you to sanity-check is the **shape of the app**, since that's the one real choice with trade-offs.

### The big decision: what kind of app
A **local app you run on your own machine and use in your browser**. There's a small background program (that you launch) which stores everything and fetches page previews; the app itself opens in a browser tab. Nothing goes to the cloud, no login — it stays exactly within the "just me, my device" scope you confirmed.

**Why not a pure in-browser app?** Two of your own requirements force this: browsers *block* a page from fetching previews (description/icon/image) off other websites, and reliable local storage with fast search is much sturdier with a small local backend. So a thin local program handles those, and you still just open one thing.

A downside to name: it's "launch the app, then open the browser," not a single double-click icon. If you'd rather have a true double-click desktop app, that's a **Tauri/Electron** wrapper — I flagged it in research as an easy later addition, or we can commit to it now. Your call.

### How your trickier requirements are handled
- **Saving stays instant** — the bookmark saves right away; the description/icon/image fill in a moment later in the background, so a slow or dead page never blocks or fails a save.
- **Duplicates** — every address is boiled down to a canonical form (`example.com` = `https://example.com/`) and the database itself refuses a second copy; saving a match opens the existing one.
- **Search** — the exact "recipes OR dinner, but NOT dessert" example is written into the filter contract as a worked example and a test.
- **"Select all showing"** — the plan is explicit that it only ever acts on what the current view shows; archived/hidden items can't be swept.
- **Saved searches** store the *filter*, not a frozen list, so they re-run live.
- **Notes** are stored as simple markdown (headings/bullets/links) and sanitized so odd pasted markup degrades to plain text instead of breaking the page.

### Proposed toolset (the "how")
TypeScript throughout · small local web server + SQLite file for storage/search · React for the interface · automated tests (unit + one end-to-end flow per user story).

### Your options at this gate
- ✅ **Approve** → I proceed to `speckit-tasks` (the actionable task breakdown), then bring that back before any implementation.
- 🖥️ **Adjust a choice** — most likely: *"make it a real double-click desktop app"*, or a different toolset — and I'll revise the plan.
- ✏️ Any other concern and we stay here.

Two questions worth your explicit nod:
1. Is **"launch a local app + open in browser"** acceptable, or do you want a **double-click desktop app** instead?
2. Any preference on the **toolset**, or happy to leave that to me?

How shall we proceed?

On your two questions:

1. Honestly, "start the app and *then* open a browser tab" sounds a little fiddly for something I'll pop into every day. My gut says a proper double-click app I can just open would feel more like a real thing I own. That said, I trust you that it's an easy addition later — so I'm fine starting with the simpler version *if* it saves real time now and doesn't box us in. I'll leave the timing to you; just don't let it slip away entirely.

2. No preference on the tools — that's your department. Go with whatever you'd stand behind.

One thing did occur to me now that you've said it all lives in a single file on my own machine: what happens if that machine dies, or I get a new laptop? I'd hate to lose the whole collection. Is there a way for me to get my bookmarks out — a backup, or something I could carry over and load back in? I'm not asking for cloud sync, just some peace of mind that they're not trapped where one broken computer wipes them out.

Otherwise the plan makes sense to me and matches what we agreed. Sort that last worry and I'm happy to approve.

Everything's updated and consistent. Constitution re-check still PASS. Here's where things stand.

## ✅ Your data-safety worry — solved (in the spec, then the plan)

Because this was a genuinely new capability, it went into the **spec** first (Story 6, `FR-026`–`FR-030`, `SC-008`/`SC-009`), then flowed into the plan.

**What you get:**
- **Export** — one click produces a **single portable file** (an open, human-readable format — not a proprietary blob you could get locked out of). You store it wherever you like: external drive, a cloud folder, a USB stick.
- **Import** — on the same machine *or a brand-new laptop*, load that one file and your whole collection comes back — bookmarks, tags, notes, read-later/archived flags, and saved searches all intact.
- **Safe re-import** — importing into a collection that already has some of the same links **merges instead of duplicating** (same normalized-address rule as before) and tells you "X added, Y already present."
- **Never corrupts** — a bad or wrong file is rejected up front and applied all-or-nothing, so a failed import **leaves your existing collection untouched**.

To be clear on the boundary you drew: this is **manual backup you trigger**, not automatic scheduled backup, and still **no cloud sync** — exactly "peace of mind, not sync."

## 🖥️ Desktop app — recorded so it can't slip
I've written a **tracked roadmap note** into the plan: v1 ships as the simpler "launch + browser" version to save real build time now, and the architecture is deliberately chosen so wrapping it into a **true double-click desktop app** later reuses the same core code unchanged. It's a documented fast-follow, not dropped.

`spec.md` (Story 6 + FR-026–030 + SC-008/009), `plan.md` (backup service/UI, desktop-wrapper note), `contracts/rest-api.md` (export/import endpoints), `data-model.md` (Export File), `quickstart.md` (US6 validation).

If the dates carry over, then ✅ **approved** — go ahead to the task breakdown. This all matches what I wanted.

All 23 tasks for Phases 1–3 are done and checked off. No post-implement hooks configured. **Stopping here for your checkpoint, as agreed** — I have not started Phase 4.

## 🎯 Checkpoint: the US1 MVP is built and working

**"Save a web address → see it as a card with a live preview."** That whole slice runs today.

### What works (verified, not just written)
- **Save** a URL → it's stored and appears newest-first as a card.
- **Auto-preview** — a background fetch pulls the page title/description/icon/image and the card fills in a moment later (verified against a live page: fetched "Example Domain", status → done). A slow/dead page never blocks the save — it just stays a plain card.
- **Address cleanup** — `example.com` is saved as `https://example.com/`.
- **Bad input** — gibberish is rejected with a message, nothing saved.
- **No duplicates** — re-saving the same address returns your existing bookmark instead of making a copy.
- **Opening** — a card's title is a real link that opens the page in a new tab.

### Quality gate
- **22 automated tests pass** (URL rules, metadata parsing, and the create/dedupe/enrich API flow).
- Type-check clean; the SPA builds; the backend boots and serves the app end-to-end.
- One honest caveat: the **Playwright end-to-end test (T016) is written but I couldn't execute it here** — this environment doesn't have the browser binaries installed. The underlying behaviour is covered by the integration tests; I'll run the e2e suite once we're somewhere it can install browsers.

### How to click around yourself
```bash
npm install       # already done here
npm run dev        # backend on :8787, app on http://localhost:5173
```
Then open **http://localhost:5173**, paste a few URLs, and watch the cards populate. (Your bookmarks persist in a local file under `~/.bookmark-manager/`.)

### What's deliberately NOT here yet
Search/filter, read-later, archive, editing, tags, saved searches, and backup/import — those are Phases 4–9, exactly the "finding → backup safety net → tidying" order you approved. The `Save`-only form and single list view are intentionally minimal for this checkpoint.

---

**Over to you.** Have a click around and tell me how it *feels*:
- Does the save-and-preview flow match what you pictured?
- Anything about the card layout or the preview behaviour you'd change now, before I build the rest on top?
